Dixon Test

Source: R/stats.R
dixon_test.Rd

Performs Dixon's Q test for potential outliers in environmental monitoring data.

Usage

dixon_test(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
dixon_test(
  df,
  location_id = "location_id",
  param_name = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  analysis_result = "analysis_result",
  default_unit = "default_unit",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
dixon_test(
  df,
  type = 0,
  opposite = FALSE,
  two_sided = TRUE,
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location_id

Location column name.

param_name

Analyte column name.

sample_date

Sample date column name.

analysis_result

Analytical result column name.

default_unit

Reporting unit column name.

type

Variant of Dixon's test.

opposite

Logical indicating whether the lowest value should be tested rather than the highest value.

two_sided

Logical indicating whether a two-sided test should be performed.

keep_data_object

Logical indicating whether the complete test object should be retained in the output.

Value

A tibble containing one row per outlier evaluation group.

Details

`dixon_test()` is an S3 generic that supports both raw `data.frame` inputs and `env_schema` objects.

If the input is grouped using [dplyr::group_by()], Dixon tests are performed within the existing groups. For ungrouped `env_schema` inputs, tests are performed separately for each:

  • location

  • analyte

  • analysis unit

Dixon's test is intended for relatively small sample sizes and is generally appropriate for groups containing between three and thirty observations.

Dixon's test evaluates whether the most extreme observation is statistically inconsistent with the remaining observations in the group.

The method is most appropriate for small datasets and should be interpreted cautiously for environmental monitoring programs with larger sample sizes.

Groundwater Monitoring

Dixon's and Grubbs' tests are generally most appropriate for relatively small datasets and may be sensitive to distributional assumptions.

For larger groundwater monitoring datasets, `rosner_test()` is often preferred.

env_schema Method

For `env_schema` objects, Dixon tests are performed using standardized analytical results stored in `.analysis_result`.

Grouping is determined automatically from the current `dplyr::group_by()` structure or, for ungrouped data, uses:

  • location

  • analyte

  • analysis unit

Examples

dixon_test(gw_data)

#> ℹ Nitrite + Nitrate, total
#> ,
#> Warning: Skipped incompatible unit conversion: degrees c -> degC
#> Warning: Skipped incompatible unit conversion: std -> ph
#> # A tibble: 387 × 5
#> # Groups:   location_id, param_name, .analysis_unit [387]
#>    location_id param_name           .analysis_unit alternative           p_value
#>    <chr>       <chr>                <chr>          <chr>                   <dbl>
#>  1 MW-2        Magnesium, dissolved mg/l           lowest value 26.7 is…  0.876 
#>  2 MW-2        Sodium, dissolved    mg/l           highest value 27.4 i…  0.0276
#>  3 MW-2        Potassium, dissolved mg/l           highest value 0.8 is…  0.351 
#>  4 MW-2        Chloride, total      mg/l           highest value 31.6 i…  0.861 
#>  5 MW-2        Sulfate, total       mg/l           highest value 200 is…  0.0635
#>  6 MW-2        Fluoride, total      mg/l           highest value 1 is a…  0     
#>  7 MW-2        Arsenic, dissolved   ug/l           highest value 10 is …  0     
#>  8 MW-2        Barium, dissolved    ug/l           highest value 134 is…  0.0648
#>  9 MW-2        Beryllium, dissolved ug/l           NA                    NA     
#> 10 MW-2        Boron, dissolved     ug/l           lowest value 1200 is…  0.936 
#> # ℹ 377 more rows

schema <- env_schema(
  gw_data,
  location = location_id,
  sample_date = sample_date,
  analyte = param_name,
  result = analysis_result,
  unit = default_unit
)
